exposure: hospital management from day of preterm premature rupture of membranes (p-PROM)
standardized conservative management at home after 48 hours of hospitalization
outcome: latency time from diagnosis to delivery
outcomes at 24 months of corrected age
cohort: 41 women with singleton or twin pregnancies complicated by p-PROM at less than 30 weeks of gestation without signs of infection.
finding: Conservative home management of p-PROM based on a standardized protocol resulted in longer latency, higher gestational age at delivery, higher neonatal weight, better Apgar scores, and shorter neonatal hospitalization compared to hospital management.
birth_weight: lower in the hospital management group
